newsitem.title: SPAIN: Madrid stocks end higher, Wall St tempers gains.
newsitem.headline: Madrid stocks end higher, Wall St tempers gains.

text.p: Madrid stocks ended up in line with major European markets but were pulled off their highs by a weak tone on Wall Street, dealers said.
Dealers predicted continued volatility in the short term.
The general index closed up 3.16 points or 0.86 percent at 467.41.
The Ibex-35 index of leading shares was up 37.39 points or 0.71 percent to 5,333.92.
Dealers said volume was moderate with about 58 billion pesetas changing hands.
"The trend in foreign markets has calmed Spanish stocks but in the short term we are going to continue the fluctuations seen in the last sessions," one dealer said.
Among individual stocks, electronics producer Amper was the leading gainer on the Ibex with an 8.3 percent rise and almost 950,000 shares traded.
Energy group Repsol added 50 pesetas to end at 5,580 after news the privatisation of the government's final 10 percent stake in the company may be sooner than originally anticipated.
Most of the large banks were up less than one percent. Banco Santander was the top performer with a 1.78 percent gain.
Telephone operator Telefonica up 15 pesetas to 3,255. In the electricity sector, Endesa gained 160 pesetas to end at 8,670.
